cuts.raw_narration: Kite, the silver-haired hunter in the wide-brimmed cap, warns the group about the chimera-ant queen he has been tracking: judging by the size of the claw, she is at least two meters long and could eat a human in no time. His truck rolls off down a dusty road toward a green forest on the horizon, carrying that warning into the countryside where the story is about to land.

The scene drops into that countryside. A dark-haired boy of about nine, Kurt, freezes in a sunlit meadow with a wooden stick in his hand as a large purple-patterned snake rears up in front of him. Behind him his little pink-haired sister, Reina, clutches a wicker basket and cowers. "It's fine. Stay close to me, Reina. I'll keep you safe. That's what big brothers are for, right?" Kurt tells her, then swings the stick and drives the snake back. It hisses, coils, and finally slithers away through the tall grass. Kurt lowers the stick, sweating and panting, and lets a relieved smile break across his face as Reina peeks out from behind him.

That evening, inside their candlelit thatched-roof home, Kurt, Reina, and their purple-haired mother sit around the low table. She reaches out warmly: "That was very brave what you did for your sister. You're truly a young man now, Kurt. You're already so reliable, at only nine years old. And that's why I want you to continue to look after Reina. I'm counting on you." Kurt straightens up and answers with a bright, determined grin: "I promise that I'll keep both of you safe no matter what happens, okay?" The camera holds on his happy face — and then that smile slowly cross-fades into dark, jointed insect legs stepping through a black tunnel lined with glowing green pods. The queen's nest, quietly answering his promise.

Later that night, we return to the small bedroom where Kurt, Reina, and their older brother Amaro lie side by side under blankets. Kurt sits up and looks down at his sleeping sister with the same protective softness from earlier. Carrying his promise forward, he whispers his plan: they will take Amaro and go fishing at the river, cook the catch, and surprise their mother with dinner. Reina wakes with sleepy green eyes and a warm smile up at her brother.

The next morning, sunlight glitters on a wide riverbank at the edge of the forest. Kurt walks along the water carrying a bamboo fishing rod, chatting cheerfully with Reina, who trots beside him holding a woven basket already brimming with fresh fish — their surprise for their mother. Mid-step, a huge dark-red spiked leg slams down into the grass right in front of them. The children stop dead. Reina's face crumples in terror and the basket slips from her fingers, spilling silver fish across the ground. Above them, a stalk-eyed, spiny insect head — the Chimera Ant Queen — leans down to inspect what it has cornered.

The queen towers over them, jaws parting to show rows of yellow teeth. Trembling and crying, Reina clutches at Kurt's side. Kurt swallows his own fear, steps forward exactly the way he did with the snake, and raises the little fishing rod like a weapon between his sister and the monster — tears streaming down his face as he screams and swings at her. It is nothing. The queen rears back and lunges. The screen cuts to the floor of her dark lair, where Kurt's small shirt and Reina's yellow hair bow lie discarded in the dirt beneath the hanging green pods. Above them, the Chimera Ant Queen grins with sharp human-like teeth, savoring the taste. "She's delicious and so nutritious. The best fodder. I must consume more of this species."
